classification.difficultyReason: The student tests the two specified zeros, then uses the explicitly cued leading and constant coefficients to infer the remaining linear factor.

content.prompt: Show that $P(x)=3x^3-5x^2-26x-8$ is divisible by both $(x-4)$ and $(3x+1)$. By considering the leading term and constant term, express $P(x)$ as a product of three linear factors and hence solve $P(x)=0$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(4)&=3(4)^3-5(4)^2-26(4)-8\\&=192-80-104-8\\&=0\\P\left(-\frac13\right)&=3\left(-\frac13\right)^3-5\left(-\frac13\right)^2-26\left(-\frac13\right)-8\\&=-\frac19-\frac59+\frac{26}{3}-8\\&=0\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $(x-4)$ and $(3x+1)$ are factors of $P(x)$.
Write $P(x)=(x-4)(3x+1)(x+c)$.
The leading coefficient is $3\times1=3$, which matches. The constant term gives
$$\begin{align*}(-4)(1)c&=-8\\c&=2\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-4)(3x+1)(x+2)\\(x-4)(3x+1)(x+2)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law,
$$x=4,\ -\frac13,\ -2.$$
